children.title: Root-Mean-Field Correspondence

children.title: Noisy Root-Finding Models
children.top_down_role: Root targets accessed through stochastic observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Root-Finding Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased stochastic-oracle model for finite-dimensional root finding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathbb{R}^d\times\Xi\to\mathbb{R}^d\) be measurable, let \(\xi\) have law \(P\), and suppose \(H(x,\xi)\) is integrable for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\). Define the mean field by \(h(x)=\mathbb{E}[H(x,\xi)]\). A noisy root-finding model seeks \(x^\star\in\mathbb{R}^d\) satisfying \(h(x^\star)=0\), while permitting access only to samples \(Y_{k+1}=H(x_k,\xi_{k+1})\). With \(\mathcal{F}_k\) denoting the information available before sampling, the canonical oracle condition is \(\mathbb{E}[Y_{k+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_k]=h(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noisy root problem seeks a zero of an expected vector field using conditionally unbiased random observations of that field.
assumptions_latex: \(H(x,\xi)\) is measurable and integrable for every \(x\).
\(\xi_{k+1}\) is sampled so that the stated conditional-unbiasedness identity holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\) solves the model exactly when \(\mathbb{E}[H(x^\star,\xi)]=0\).

notation.meaning: random observation of the vector field at x

children.title: Mean-Field Equation Models
children.top_down_role: Deterministic mean fields induced by stochastic observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Mean-Field Equation Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean equation induced by an integrable stochastic observation map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Xi,\mathcal{A},P)\) be a probability space and let \(H:D\times\Xi\to\mathbb{R}^d\), where \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), be measurable with \(\mathbb{E}[\|H(x,\xi)\|]<\infty\) for every \(x\in D\). The associated mean field is \(h:D\to\mathbb{R}^d\), \(h(x)=\int_\Xi H(x,z)\,P(dz)\). The mean-field equation model is the deterministic equation \(h(x)=0\); its solution set is \(Z(h)=\{x\in D:h(x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mean-field model replaces random observations by their expectation and asks for a zero of the resulting deterministic vector field.
assumptions_latex: \(H(x,\xi)\) is measurable and integrable for each \(x\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z(h)=\{x\in D:\mathbb{E}[H(x,\xi)]=0\}\).

notation.meaning: zero set of the mean field

children.title: Root–Equilibrium Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural links between mean-field roots and limiting equilibria.

knowledge_statements.title: Root–Equilibrium Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equilibria of the autonomous mean-field ODE with negative drift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be open and let \(h:D\to\mathbb{R}^d\) be continuous. Consider the autonomous mean-field ordinary differential equation \(\dot{x}(t)=-h(x(t))\). A point \(x^\star\in D\) is an equilibrium, meaning that the constant curve \(x(t)=x^\star\) satisfies the equation for every \(t\geq0\), if and only if \(h(x^\star)=0\). Consequently, the equilibrium set of the mean-field flow equals the root set \(Z(h)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is a root of the mean field exactly when it is an equilibrium of the ODE driven by the negative mean field.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Eq}(\dot{x}=-h(x))=Z(h)\).

notation.meaning: equilibrium set of the displayed ODE

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: substitution of a constant trajectory gives the exact root–equilibrium equivalence

children.title: Expected-Risk Objectives
children.top_down_role: Optimization objectives expressed through expectations over random data.

knowledge_statements.title: Expected-Risk Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Population objective obtained by averaging a measurable loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal{Z},\mathcal{A},P)\) be a probability space, let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, and let \(\ell:X\times\mathcal{Z}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be measurable in its data argument. Whenever the expectation is well defined, the expected-risk or population objective is \(F(x)=\mathbb{E}_{Z\sim P}[\ell(x,Z)]\). The expected-risk optimization problem is \(\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\), with solution set \(X^\star=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected-risk minimization chooses a decision minimizing the population average of its loss on a random data point.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell(x,\cdot)\) is measurable and has a well-defined expectation for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^\star=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\mathbb{E}[\ell(x,Z)]\).

knowledge_statements.title: Population Objective Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity and smoothness inherited by an expected-risk objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be convex and let \(F(x)=\mathbb{E}[\ell(x,Z)]\) be finite on \(X\). If \(\ell(\cdot,z)\) is convex for \(P\)-almost every \(z\), then \(F\) is convex. If, additionally, \(\ell(\cdot,z)\) is differentiable and has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient on \(X\) for \(P\)-almost every \(z\), with differentiation interchangeable with expectation, then \(F\) is differentiable, \(
abla F(x)=\mathbb{E}[
abla_x\ell(x,Z)]\), and \(
abla F\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise convexity and a uniform gradient-Lipschitz bound pass from sample losses to the population risk when differentiation and expectation may be interchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is convex and \(F\) is finite on \(X\).
\(\ell(\cdot,z)\) is convex and differentiable for almost every \(z\).
Differentiation commutes with expectation, and each sample gradient is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(F\) is convex, \(
abla F=\mathbb{E}[
abla_x\ell(\cdot,Z)]\), and \(\|
abla F(x)-
abla F(y)\|\leq L\|x-y\|\).

children.title: Sampled First-Order Access
children.top_down_role: Gradient or subgradient information obtained from sampled observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampled First-Order Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditionally unbiased stochastic first-order oracle for convex population risk, with a differentiable finite-variance specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty and convex, let \(F(x)=\mathbb{E}[\ell(x,Z)]\), and suppose \(\ell(\cdot,z)\) is proper and convex for almost every \(z\). Let \(\partial\) denote the convex subdifferential, and let \(\mathcal{F}_k\) contain the algorithmic history through \(x_k\). Sampled first-order access returns an integrable vector \(G_{k+1}=g(x_k,Z_{k+1})\), where \(g(x,z)\in\partial_x\ell(x,z)\), subject to \(\mathbb{E}[G_{k+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_k]\in\partial F(x_k)\). If \(F\) and the sampled losses are differentiable at the queried points, this condition becomes \(\mathbb{E}[G_{k+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_k]=\nabla F(x_k)\). In that differentiable specialization, a finite-noise condition is \(\mathbb{E}[\|G_{k+1}-\nabla F(x_k)\|^2\mid\mathcal{F}_k]\leq\sigma^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampled first-order access returns an integrable sample subgradient whose conditional mean is a convex subgradient of the population risk; in the differentiable specialization it is an unbiased gradient and may additionally satisfy a bounded conditional-variance condition.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell(\cdot,z)\) is proper and convex for almost every \(z\).
\(g(x,z)\in\partial_x\ell(x,z)\) is measurable, and the oracle output is conditionally integrable.
The variance bound is imposed only in the differentiable specialization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[G_{k+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_k]\in\partial F(x_k)\), with equality to \(\nabla F(x_k)\) in the differentiable specialization.

notation.meaning: algorithmic history before the next sample
conditional noise-variance bound in the differentiable specialization

children.title: Finite-Sum Objectives
children.top_down_role: Objectives assembled from a finite collection of component losses.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sum Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformly weighted finite collection of component objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty and let \(f_i:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) for \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). A finite-sum objective has the form \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), and the associated optimization problem is \(\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\). More generally, positive weights \(w_i\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^n w_i=1\) define \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n w_i f_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-sum problem minimizes an average, or weighted average, of finitely many component functions.
assumptions_latex: The finite sum is well defined on its effective domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}F(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) in the uniform case.

children.title: Empirical-Risk Objectives
children.top_down_role: Sample-average objectives arising from finite datasets.

knowledge_statements.title: Empirical-Risk Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample average loss for a fixed observed dataset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)\in\mathcal{Z}^n\) be an observed sample, let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), and let \(\ell:X\times\mathcal{Z}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a loss. The empirical risk is \(\widehat F_S(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\ell(x,z_i)\). Empirical-risk minimization returns any \(\widehat x_S\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\widehat F_S(x)\), provided this set is nonempty. Thus empirical risk is a finite-sum objective with components \(f_i(x)=\ell(x,z_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Empirical-risk minimization fits a decision by minimizing the average loss over the observed sample.
assumptions_latex: \(S=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)\) is fixed when defining the empirical objective.
\(\ell(x,z_i)\) is well defined for every feasible \(x\) and sample point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x_S\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\ell(x,z_i)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Component-Sampling Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased gradient estimation by importance-weighted component sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), where every \(f_i\) is differentiable at \(x\). Choose an index \(I\) with probabilities \(p_i>0\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1\), and define \(G(x,I)=(n p_I)^{-1}
abla f_I(x)\). Then \(\mathbb{E}[G(x,I)\mid x]=
abla F(x)\). Under uniform sampling, \(p_i=1/n\), the estimator reduces to \(G(x,I)=
abla f_I(x)\). The same identity holds conditionally at an iterate when the sampling probabilities are measurable before drawing \(I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling one component and applying the appropriate importance weight gives an unbiased estimator of the finite-sum gradient.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i\) is differentiable at the queried point for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[(n p_I)^{-1}\nabla f_I(x)\mid x]=\nabla F(x)\).

children.title: Stochastic Monotone Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Random operator inclusion models with monotonicity structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Monotone Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone inclusion with an expectation-valued stochastic operator component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{H}\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:\mathcal{H}\rightrightarrows\mathcal{H}\) be maximally monotone, and let \(B:\mathcal{H}\times\Xi\to\mathcal{H}\) be measurable with \(B(x,\xi)\) integrable for each \(x\). Define \(\overline B(x)=\mathbb{E}[B(x,\xi)]\), and suppose \(\overline B\) is monotone. The stochastic monotone inclusion problem is to find \(x^\star\in\mathcal{H}\) such that \(0\in A(x^\star)+\overline B(x^\star)\), using sampled evaluations of \(B(x,\xi)\) rather than exact evaluations of \(\overline B(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic monotone inclusion seeks a zero of a set-valued monotone operator plus an expected monotone field accessed through samples.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximally monotone on the real Hilbert space \(\mathcal{H}\).
\(B(x,\xi)\) is measurable and integrable for each \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname{zer}(A+\overline B)\).

children.title: Randomized Fixed-Point Problems
children.top_down_role: Fixed-point targets accessed through randomized operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Fixed-Point Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common fixed-point feasibility with operators sampled from a finite or countable discrete support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{H}\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(\mathcal{I}_P\) be finite or countable, and let \(\{T_i:\mathcal{H}\to\mathcal{H}\}_{i\in\mathcal{I}_P}\) be a family of operators. Let \(I\) be an \(\mathcal{I}_P\)-valued random index with \(p_i=\mathbb{P}(I=i)>0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal{I}_P\). The randomized common fixed-point problem is to find \(x^\star\in\bigcap_{i\in\mathcal{I}_P}\operatorname{Fix}(T_i)\). Under the positive-probability assumption, this is equivalent to \(T_Ix^\star=x^\star\) almost surely. Randomized access evaluates only \(T_{I_k}\) at iteration \(k\), and consistency requires \(\bigcap_{i\in\mathcal{I}_P}\operatorname{Fix}(T_i)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite or countable collection in which every operator has positive sampling probability, a randomized fixed-point problem seeks a point fixed by every sampled operator; equivalently, it is fixed by a random operator almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\bigcap_{i\in\mathcal{I}_P}\operatorname{Fix}(T_i)\) if and only if \(T_Ix^\star=x^\star\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: positive probability of sampling index i

children.title: Resolvent-Based Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Connections between monotone inclusions and fixed-point representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent-Based Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equivalence between monotone zeros and resolvent fixed points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{H}\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:\mathcal{H}\rightrightarrows\mathcal{H}\) be maximally monotone, and let \(\gamma>0\). Its resolvent is the everywhere-defined single-valued operator \(J_{\gamma A}=(\operatorname{Id}+\gamma A)^{-1}\). For every \(x\in\mathcal{H}\), \(0\in A(x)\) if and only if \(x=J_{\gamma A}(x)\). Hence \(\operatorname{zer}(A)=\operatorname{Fix}(J_{\gamma A})\), converting the monotone inclusion into a fixed-point problem without changing its solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero of a maximally monotone operator is exactly a fixed point of any positive-parameter resolvent of that operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{zer}(A)=\operatorname{Fix}(J_{\gamma A})\).

notation.meaning: resolvent of A with parameter gamma
identity operator on the Hilbert space
set of x satisfying zero in A(x)

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Recursive Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time, set-valued stochastic approximation with additive perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H:\mathbb{R}^d\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^d\) be set-valued, let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\geq 0}\) be a filtration, and let \((\alpha_k)_{k\geq 0}\) be positive step sizes. A stochastic recursive inclusion is an adapted process \((x_k)_{k\geq 0}\) satisfying
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_k(v_k+M_{k+1}+b_k),\qquad v_k\in H(x_k),
\]
where \(v_k\) and \(b_k\) are \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable and \(M_{k+1}\) is \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable. Constraints may be represented by taking \(H=G+N_C\), where \(N_C\) is the normal-cone mapping of a closed convex set \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recursive inclusion updates an adapted iterate using any selected mean-field direction, stochastic noise, and bias; normal-cone terms can encode convex constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(H:\mathbb{R}^d\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^d\) has nonempty values along the iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\in x_k-\alpha_k\bigl(H(x_k)+M_{k+1}+b_k\bigr)\).

notation.meaning: normal-cone mapping of the constraint set

children.title: Unbiased Gradient Oracles

knowledge_statements.title: Unbiased Gradient Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional unbiasedness for differentiable stochastic first-order optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and let \(x_k\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable. A random oracle output \(G_{k+1}\) is an unbiased gradient oracle at \(x_k\) when \(G_{k+1}\) is integrable, \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable, and
\[
\mathbb E[G_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f(x_k)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Equivalently, the oracle error \(M_{k+1}:=G_{k+1}-\nabla f(x_k)\) is conditionally centered. Unbiasedness alone imposes no finite-variance or independence requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given the current information, the oracle’s expected random direction equals the exact gradient; this condition alone does not ensure bounded variance or independence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[G_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f(x_k)\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: information available before the next oracle call
oracle error relative to the exact gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Unbiased Subgradient Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional unbiasedness for convex, possibly nonsmooth objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper convex, and let \(x_k\in\operatorname{dom}f\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable. An integrable, \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable output \(G_{k+1}\) is an unbiased subgradient oracle at \(x_k\) if there exists an \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable selection \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) such that
\[
\mathbb E[G_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]=g_k\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Thus conditional expectation must belong to \(\partial f(x_k)\); individual oracle realizations need not themselves be subgradients unless separately required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conditional mean of the random oracle output must be a valid convex subgradient at the current iterate, although individual samples need not be subgradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[G_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\in\partial f(x_k)\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential of f at x

children.title: Conditional Centering Regimes
children.top_down_role: Filtration-relative centering structures for first-order observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Centering Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Centering relative to the algorithm’s pre-oracle filtration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\geq0}\) be a filtration and let \(M_{k+1}\) be an integrable, \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable oracle error. The conditional-centering condition is
\[
\mathbb E[M_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\quad\text{almost surely for every }k.
\]
If an oracle has the decomposition \(G_{k+1}=h(x_k)+M_{k+1}\), with \(x_k\) and \(h(x_k)\) measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_k\), then conditional centering is equivalent to \(\mathbb E[G_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]=h(x_k)\). It permits dependence on the past through the conditional distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle noise is conditionally centered when its expectation, given all pre-call information, is zero; it may still depend on the past.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[M_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\) almost surely for every \(k\).

notation.meaning: oracle error revealed after iteration k

children.title: Biased-Inexact Oracle Regimes
children.top_down_role: Persistent, vanishing, and controllable oracle inexactness regimes.

children.title: Persistent Oracle Bias
children.top_down_role: Nonvanishing systematic error in stochastic oracle outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Oracle Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonvanishing conditional mean error along an infinite subsequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an integrable oracle admits
\[
G_{k+1}=h(x_k)+b_k+M_{k+1},\qquad b_k:=\mathbb E[G_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]-h(x_k),
\]
where \(x_k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable and \(\mathbb E[M_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\). The oracle has persistent bias along the generated trajectory if
\[
\limsup_{k\to\infty}\lVert b_k\rVert>0
\]
with positive probability. A uniformly persistent regime satisfies \(\lVert b_k\rVert\geq\varepsilon\) eventually almost surely for some deterministic \(\varepsilon>0\). Persistence concerns conditional mean error, not random variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle bias is persistent when the conditional mean error fails to approach zero; a stronger uniform form stays bounded away from zero eventually.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\lVert\mathbb E[G_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]-h(x_k)\rVert>0\) with positive probability.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed condition is internally coherent, but "persistent bias" is not governed by a unique convention: positive-probability limsup persistence and eventual almost-sure uniform separation are materially different regimes. No source is supplied to establish that the selected convention matches this leaf.

children.title: Vanishing Oracle Bias
children.top_down_role: Systematic oracle error that decreases over time or accuracy levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Oracle Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotically unbiased conditional mean directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G_{k+1}\) be an integrable stochastic oracle at the \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable point \(x_k\), and let \(h(x_k)\) be the intended \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable direction. Define
\[
b_k:=\mathbb E[G_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]-h(x_k).
\]
The oracle has vanishing bias along the generated trajectory if \(\lVert b_k\rVert\to0\) almost surely. For stochastic-approximation updates with step sizes \(\alpha_k\), the stronger weighted-summability regime is
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k\lVert b_k\rVert<\infty\quad\text{almost surely},
\]
which controls cumulative bias and implies vanishing bias when additional regularity prevents isolated spikes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conditional mean oracle error vanishes along the iterates; weighted summability is a stronger compatibility condition controlling its cumulative effect.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\mathbb E[G_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]-h(x_k)\rVert\to0\) almost surely.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The almost-sure limit definition is coherent, but the weighted-summability condition is not unconditionally stronger than pointwise vanishing: either property may hold without the other for general positive step sizes and bias sequences. The stated additional regularity is unspecified, and no source fixes the intended bias regime or its relation to summability.

children.title: Controllable Oracle Inexactness
children.top_down_role: Oracle accuracy governed by computational or sampling effort.

knowledge_statements.title: Controllable Oracle Inexactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle error bounded by a user-selected accuracy parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) be a target direction and let \(G(x,\xi,\eta)\) denote an oracle queried at accuracy \(\eta>0\). The oracle has controllable inexactness if there is a deterministic modulus \(\delta:(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\), with \(\delta(\eta)\to0\) as \(\eta\downarrow0\), such that
\[
\bigl\lVert\mathbb E[G(x,\xi,\eta)]-h(x)\bigr\rVert\leq\delta(\eta)
\]
for every admissible \(x\). Along an algorithmic sequence \((x_k,\eta_k)\), choosing \(\eta_k\downarrow0\) therefore makes the conditional mean inexactness vanish, provided the same bound holds conditionally on \(\mathcal F_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tunable accuracy parameter bounds the oracle’s mean error through a modulus that approaches zero as increasingly accurate queries are requested.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is the target direction.
\(G(x,\xi,\eta)\) is integrable for each admissible \(x\) and \(\eta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\mathbb E[G(x,\xi,\eta)]-h(x)\rVert\leq\delta(\eta)\) for every admissible \(x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The modulus-based model is a plausible condition for controllable mean inexactness, but controllable oracle accuracy is modeled in several inequivalent ways, including deterministic realization error, conditional bias, and function-model error. The unconditional expectation also leaves the law of the oracle randomness unspecified. An authoritative source is required to select and support this exact convention.

children.top_down_role: Finite-difference, simultaneous-perturbation, and smoothing-based stochastic information.

children.title: Stochastic Function-Value Oracles
children.top_down_role: Noisy objective-value information without direct derivatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Function-Value Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noisy zeroth-order observations with specified conditional mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), and let \(x_k\) be an \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable query. A stochastic function-value oracle returns an integrable scalar \(Y_{k+1}\), measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\), having the decomposition
\[
Y_{k+1}=f(x_k)+b_k+\varepsilon_{k+1},
\qquad \mathbb E[\varepsilon_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]=0.
\]
Here \(b_k\) is the conditional bias. The oracle is conditionally unbiased when \(b_k=0\) almost surely. This definition supplies function values only; derivative estimates require multiple queries, perturbations, or structural assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic value oracle returns a noisy scalar whose conditional mean is the objective value plus a possible bias; it provides no derivative directly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[Y_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]=f(x_k)+b_k\) almost surely.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The decomposition is a coherent definition of a biased stochastic function-value oracle and the definition content kind fits the leaf. No source or inspectable locator is supplied for this zeroth-order oracle convention, so the record cannot be accepted under the evidence requirements.

children.title: Finite-Difference Estimators
children.top_down_role: Derivative surrogates formed from perturbed function evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Difference Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise central differences formed from stochastic value queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), radius \(\mu>0\), and coordinate vectors \(e_1,\ldots,e_d\), the coordinatewise central finite-difference estimator based on value-oracle outputs \(Y(\cdot)\) is
\[
\widehat g_\mu(x)=\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{Y(x+\mu e_i)-Y(x-\mu e_i)}{2\mu}e_i.
\]
It uses \(2d\) function-value queries. If the paired observations are conditionally unbiased, then its conditional mean equals the central-difference vector of \(f\). If \(f\) is three times continuously differentiable near the queried points with bounded third directional derivatives, each coordinate has deterministic truncation error of order \(\mu^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Central coordinate differences use two noisy value queries per coordinate; their mean reproduces the central difference, with quadratic truncation error under bounded third derivatives.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is defined at \(x\pm\mu e_i\) for every \(i\).
The paired value-oracle observations are conditionally unbiased.
For the error order, \(f\) has bounded third coordinate derivatives near the query points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\widehat g_\mu(x)\mid x]=\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{f(x+\mu e_i)-f(x-\mu e_i)}{2\mu}e_i\), using \(2d\) value queries.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed coordinatewise central-difference representation and the 2d query count are standard, but the conditioning notation "given x" does not specify the sigma-field or whether paired query noise shares randomness. The coordinatewise order claim also requires a precisely stated uniform third-derivative bound. No source supports the estimator version or error statement.

children.title: Simultaneous-Perturbation Estimators
children.top_down_role: Random-direction estimators using coordinated coordinate perturbations.

knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous-Perturbation Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-query symmetric estimator using one random multivariate perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Delta=(\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_d)\) have almost surely nonzero components, let \(\mu>0\), and let \(Y(\cdot)\) be a stochastic value oracle. The two-sided simultaneous-perturbation estimator is
\[
\widehat g_{\mu,i}(x)=\frac{Y(x+\mu\Delta)-Y(x-\mu\Delta)}{2\mu\Delta_i},\qquad i=1,\ldots,d.
\]
It requires two function-value queries independently of \(d\). When the observations are conditionally unbiased and \(\Delta\) is independent of their centered noise, its conditional mean is the corresponding randomized symmetric-difference direction; convergence to \(\nabla f(x)\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\) requires suitable smoothness and perturbation-moment conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single random vector perturbs all coordinates simultaneously, producing a two-query gradient estimate whose small-radius validity requires smoothness and controlled inverse perturbation moments.
assumptions_latex: The two value observations are conditionally unbiased.
The perturbation is independent of the centered observation noise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat g_{\mu,i}(x)=[Y(x+\mu\Delta)-Y(x-\mu\Delta)]/(2\mu\Delta_i)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,d\), using two value queries.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed two-sided SPSA estimator and dimension-independent two-query count are recognizable, but nonzero perturbation components alone do not provide the inverse-moment conditions needed for its expectation or limiting behavior. The phrase "conditional mean" does not state whether conditioning includes the sampled perturbation. An authoritative SPSA source is required to fix these details.

children.title: Smoothing-Based Oracles
children.top_down_role: Stochastic derivative information induced by smoothed objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Smoothing-Based Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-point gradient representation for spherical randomized smoothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be locally integrable, let \(U\) be uniform on the Euclidean unit ball, and define the ball-smoothed objective \(f_\mu(x):=\mathbb E[f(x+\mu U)]\) for \(\mu>0\). If \(V\) is uniform on the unit sphere and the relevant expectations are finite, then
\[
\nabla f_\mu(x)=\frac{d}{2\mu}\mathbb E\bigl[(f(x+\mu V)-f(x-\mu V))V\bigr].
\]
Replacing the two exact values by conditionally unbiased stochastic value-oracle outputs yields an unbiased oracle for \(\nabla f_\mu(x)\), rather than generally for \(\nabla f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random spherical perturbations give an unbiased two-point gradient oracle for a ball-smoothed objective, not generally for the original objective.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is locally integrable and the displayed expectations are finite.
\(U\) is uniform on the unit ball and \(V\) is uniform on the unit sphere.
The two stochastic value observations are conditionally unbiased.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\frac{d}{2\mu}(Y(x+\mu V)-Y(x-\mu V))V\mid x]=\nabla f_\mu(x)\).

notation.meaning: uniform random vector on the unit ball
uniform random vector on the unit sphere

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalization is consistent with the usual symmetric two-point representation for uniform-ball smoothing, but local integrability and finiteness alone do not clearly guarantee a classical gradient at every stated x; the identity may initially hold only almost everywhere or under stronger regularity. The conditional unbiasedness of two stochastic evaluations also needs a specified conditioning and sampling model. A source is necessary to determine the correct hypotheses and scope.

children.title: Noise Dependence Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Noise classifications determined by filtration, bias, temporal dependence, state dependence, and delayed information.

children.title: Martingale-Difference Noise
children.top_down_role: The canonical conditionally centered noise regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Martingale-Difference Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical adapted, conditionally mean-zero stochastic-approximation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\geq0}\) be a filtration. A sequence \((M_{k+1})_{k\geq0}\) is a martingale-difference noise sequence relative to this filtration if each \(M_{k+1}\) is integrable and \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable, and
\[
\mathbb E[M_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\quad\text{almost surely for every }k.
\]
Consequently, the partial sums \(S_n:=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}M_{k+1}\) form an integrable martingale relative to \((\mathcal F_n)_{n\geq0}\). Conditional variance bounds or square integrability are additional assumptions, not part of the martingale-difference definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noise is a martingale difference when it is revealed one step ahead and has zero conditional mean; its partial sums then form a martingale.
assumptions_latex: \(M_{k+1}\) is integrable and \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[M_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\) almost surely, and \(S_n=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}M_{k+1}\) is a martingale.

children.title: Bias-Perturbation Compatibility Regimes

children.title: Controlled Oracle Bias
children.top_down_role: Quantified systematic error compatible with stochastic approximation analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Controlled Oracle Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-mean bias model for a stochastic first-order oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_k\) be adapted to a filtration \((\mathcal F_k)\), and let \(G_k\) be an integrable oracle observation at \(x_k\). Relative to a target field \(g\), the oracle has controlled bias if there exist an \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable vector \(b_k\) and a deterministic bound \(\beta_k\ge 0\) such that
\[
\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=g(x_k)+b_k,\qquad \|b_k\|\le \beta_k
\]
almost surely for every \(k\). Vanishing controlled bias additionally requires \(\beta_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle bias is controlled when its conditional mean differs from the target field by a measurable error bounded by a prescribed sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]-g(x_k)=b_k\) with \(\|b_k\|\le\beta_k\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: information available before the kth oracle observation

children.title: Summable Approximation Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Accumulated approximation errors with finite long-run influence.

knowledge_statements.title: Summable Approximation Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted summability condition for errors entering a stochastic-approximation update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider an update whose direction is perturbed from \(G_k\) to \(G_k+e_k\), with stepsize \(\alpha_k\ge0\). The approximation perturbations are summable along the update if
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k\|e_k\|<\infty
\]
almost surely. If the perturbation is already expressed as an additive iterate displacement \(d_k=\alpha_k e_k\), the equivalent condition is \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|d_k\|<\infty\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximation errors are summable when their stepsize-weighted magnitudes have finite total accumulation almost surely.
assumptions_latex: Each \(e_k\) is a finite-dimensional random vector measurable when used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k\|e_k\|<\infty\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: error in the computed oracle direction
additive iterate displacement caused by the error

children.title: Bias–Perturbation Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Joint admissibility regimes for systematic and approximation errors.

knowledge_statements.title: Bias–Perturbation Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint accumulation condition for biased and inexact stochastic directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the direction used at iteration \(k\) is \(G_k+e_k\), where \(\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=g(x_k)+b_k\), and the update scales this direction by \(\alpha_k\ge0\). Bias and approximation perturbations are compatible with the stepsizes when
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k\bigl(\|b_k\|+\|e_k\|\bigr)<\infty
\]
almost surely. This condition makes the total pathwise displacement attributable to conditional bias and approximation error finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bias and approximation error are compatible when their combined stepsize-weighted magnitude is summable almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k(\|b_k\|+\|e_k\|)<\infty\) almost surely.

children.title: Exogenous Markovian Noise
children.top_down_role: Observation noise driven by an external Markov process.

knowledge_statements.title: Exogenous Markovian Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Markov observations whose transition law is independent of the optimization iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((Z_k)\) be a time-homogeneous Markov chain on a measurable state space with transition kernel \(P\), and let the oracle be \(G_k=H(x_k,Z_k)\). The noise is exogenous Markovian when
\[
\mathbb P(Z_{k+1}\in A\mid\mathcal F_k,x_k)=P(Z_k,A)
\]
for every measurable \(A\), so the iterate does not control the chain. If \(P\) has invariant law \(\pi\), the associated stationary mean field is \(h(x)=\int H(x,z)\,\pi(dz)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exogenous Markovian noise comes from a Markov chain whose transition kernel is unaffected by the current optimization iterate.
assumptions_latex: \((Z_k)\) is a time-homogeneous Markov chain with kernel \(P\).
\(H(x,\cdot)\) is integrable under the invariant law whenever the mean field is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z_{k+1}\mid(\mathcal F_k,x_k)\sim P(Z_k,\cdot)\), independently of the choice of \(x_k\).

notation.meaning: invariant distribution of the Markov chain

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed exogenous-kernel definition is plausible, but no citation is supplied to verify the precise filtration convention or stationary mean-field formulation.

children.title: Controlled Markov Sampling
children.top_down_role: Markov transition behavior influenced by algorithmic state or controls.

knowledge_statements.title: Controlled Markov Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Markov sampling with an iterate-indexed transition kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_x\) be a Markov transition kernel for each \(x\) in the iterate space. Sampling is controlled Markovian when an adapted pair \((x_k,Z_k)\) satisfies
\[
\mathbb P(Z_{k+1}\in A\mid\mathcal F_k)=P_{x_k}(Z_k,A)
\]
for every measurable \(A\). If each \(P_x\) admits an invariant law \(\pi_x\), then an oracle \(H(x,Z)\) has controlled stationary mean field \(h(x)=\int H(x,z)\,\pi_x(dz)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Controlled Markov sampling lets the current iterate select the transition kernel governing the next observation.
assumptions_latex: For each \(x\), \(P_x\) is a Markov kernel.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k\sim P_{x_k}(Z_k,\cdot)\).

notation.meaning: transition kernel selected by control or iterate x
invariant law of the kernel selected by x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The iterate-indexed transition-kernel definition is plausible and locally appropriate, but an authoritative source is required for the controlled-chain convention and invariant-law formulation.

children.title: Iterate-Dependent Observation Noise
children.top_down_role: Observation distributions whose behavior varies with the current iterate.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterate-Dependent Observation Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observation distributions parametrized directly by the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q_x\) be a probability kernel on an observation space, and let \(x_k\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable. Observation noise is iterate-dependent when
\[
Z_k\mid\mathcal F_k\sim Q_{x_k},\qquad G_k=H(x_k,Z_k).
\]
When the integral exists, its conditional mean field is \(h(x)=\int H(x,z)\,Q_x(dz)\), and the centered noise is \(M_k=G_k-h(x_k)\), satisfying \(\mathbb E[M_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The observation law depends on the current iterate, while subtracting its iterate-specific mean yields centered conditional noise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z_k\mid\mathcal F_k\sim Q_{x_k}\) and \(\mathbb E[G_k-h(x_k)\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\).

notation.meaning: mean oracle under the observation law at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional sampling and centering formulas are coherent, but no source verifies this exact notion or its intended distinction from controlled Markov sampling.

children.title: Mixing-Time Regimes
children.top_down_role: Temporal dependence classes organized by mixing behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixing-Time Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total-variation classification of convergence toward a Markov chain's invariant law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a Markov kernel \(P\) with invariant distribution \(\pi\), define
\[
\tau(\varepsilon)=\inf\left\{t\ge0:\sup_z\|P^t(z,\cdot)-\pi\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\varepsilon\right\}.
\]
The chain is uniformly geometrically mixing if constants \(C<\infty\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\) satisfy \(\sup_z\|P^t(z,\cdot)-\pi\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le C\rho^t\) for all \(t\). More generally, a mixing-time regime is specified by an explicit upper bound on \(\tau(\varepsilon)\) or the corresponding decay profile.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixing-time regime quantifies how rapidly every initial state approaches the invariant distribution in total variation.
assumptions_latex: Total-variation distance is defined on the chain's measurable state space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dependence regime is quantified by \(\tau(\varepsilon)\) or by a uniform decay bound for \(\|P^t(z,\cdot)-\pi\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed uniform total-variation mixing time is standard, but no citation supports the chosen uniform regime or establishes that it is the intended scope of this taxonomy leaf.

children.title: Correlated-Delayed-Asynchronous Noise Family
children.top_down_role: Dependence introduced by correlated observations, delayed information, or asynchronous execution.

children.title: Temporally Correlated Noise
children.top_down_role: Observation errors with serial dependence across iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporally Correlated Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Centered oracle errors with nontrivial dependence across iteration times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\xi_k)\) be a square-integrable, mean-zero noise sequence. It is temporally correlated when it is not an independent sequence and its lagged dependence is nontrivial; in the second-order stationary case, this may be expressed by
\[
\Gamma(\ell)=\mathbb E[\xi_{k+\ell}\xi_k^{\mathsf T}]\ne0
\]
for at least one lag \(\ell\ge1\). Temporal correlation does not by itself imply conditional centering \(\mathbb E[\xi_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1}]=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporally correlated oracle errors retain dependence across iterations, commonly witnessed by a nonzero lagged covariance.
assumptions_latex: The covariance characterization assumes second-order stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(\ell\ge1\) with \(\Gamma(\ell)\ne0\) in the stated second-order characterization.

notation.meaning: centered oracle noise at iteration k
information preceding the kth noise realization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Nonzero lag covariance is only a sufficient witness for some temporal dependence, not a characterization of all nonindependent sequences. A source is needed to fix the intended definition and second-order scope.

children.title: Delayed-Information Noise
children.top_down_role: Stochastic errors arising from stale observations or iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Delayed-Information Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient discrepancy caused by evaluating an oracle at a stale iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\tau_k\) be an integer delay satisfying \(0\le\tau_k\le k\), and suppose the direction used at time \(k\) is \(G_k=g(x_{k-\tau_k})+\xi_k\). Relative to current information, delayed-information noise is the discrepancy
\[
d_k=g(x_{k-\tau_k})-g(x_k),
\]
so that \(G_k=g(x_k)+d_k+\xi_k\). A bounded-delay regime imposes \(\tau_k\le\tau_{\max}<\infty\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A delayed oracle evaluates the target field at a stale iterate, creating a discrepancy relative to the current iterate.
assumptions_latex: The target field \(g\) is defined at both \(x_k\) and \(x_{k-\tau_k}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_k-g(x_k)=d_k+\xi_k\), where \(d_k=g(x_{k-\tau_k})-g(x_k)\).

children.title: Asynchronous-Execution Noise
children.top_down_role: Perturbations induced by unsynchronized computation or communication.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous-Execution Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stale-read and partial-write representation of asynchronous stochastic updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An asynchronous stochastic update can be represented as
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_k U_kG(\widehat x_k,\zeta_k),
\]
where \(U_k\) selects the coordinates written at event \(k\), and \(\widehat x_k\) is the possibly inconsistent vector read by the worker. Relative to the synchronous direction \(G(x_k,\zeta_k)\), execution noise is
\[
e_k=U_kG(\widehat x_k,\zeta_k)-G(x_k,\zeta_k).
\]
It combines coordinate-selection and stale-read discrepancies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous execution replaces a synchronous full update by a partial update computed from a stale or inconsistent read.
assumptions_latex: \(U_k\) is a linear coordinate-selection or write operator.
\(\widehat x_k\) contains values read before the kth write event.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_k(G(x_k,\zeta_k)+e_k)\) with the displayed execution error \(e_k\).

children.title: Coupled Dependence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where correlation, staleness, or execution effects interact.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Dependence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint dependence among sampling noise, delays, and asynchronous scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\xi_k\), \(\tau_k\), and \(U_k\) denote observation noise, delay, and update selection. They form a coupled dependence regime when their conditional joint law given the past cannot generally be factored into its conditional marginals; that is, for some \(k\),
\[
\mathcal L(\xi_k,\tau_k,U_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\ne
\mathcal L(\xi_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\otimes
\mathcal L(\tau_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\otimes
\mathcal L(U_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1}).
\]
Analysis must therefore control their joint conditional law or a joint dependence coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noise, delays, and update schedules are coupled when their joint conditional law does not factor given the past.
assumptions_latex: Regular conditional laws exist for \(\xi_k\), \(\tau_k\), and \(U_k\) given \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditional product-factorization displayed above fails for at least one iteration \(k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure of conditional product factorization is a coherent dependence condition, but no source shows that this exact three-way formulation captures the intended coupled regimes rather than only one special case.

children.title: Uniform Variance Bounds
children.top_down_role: Noise regimes with iterate-independent variance control.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Variance Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global conditional second-moment control for stochastic oracle fluctuations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G_k\) be square-integrable conditionally on \(\mathcal F_k\), and define its centered fluctuation by \(M_k=G_k-\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\). The oracle satisfies a uniform conditional variance bound if there exists a finite constant \(\sigma^2\ge0\), independent of \(k\) and the realized iterate, such that
\[
\mathbb E[\|M_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma^2
\]
almost surely for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle fluctuations have uniformly bounded conditional variance when one finite constant bounds their conditional second moments at every iteration.
assumptions_latex: The norm is fixed on the finite-dimensional oracle space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\|G_k-\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma^2\) almost surely for all \(k\).

notation.meaning: information conditioning the kth oracle call

abla f(x)\). The oracle has state-dependent variance growth if constants \(\sigma_0,\sigma_1\ge 0\) exist such that, for every admissible \(x\), \[\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\|G(x,\xi)-
abla f(x)ight\|^2\mid xight]\le \sigma_0^2+\sigma_1^2\left\|

children.title: Local Variance Control
children.top_down_role: Variance bounds restricted to neighborhoods or bounded trajectory regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Variance Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local boundedness of oracle variance without a global uniform bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be open, let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, and let \(G(x,\xi)\) be an unbiased stochastic gradient oracle. Local variance control holds when, for every \(x_0\in D\), there are a neighborhood \(U_{x_0}\subseteq D\) and a finite constant \(V_{x_0}\) such that \[\sup_{x\in U_{x_0}}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\|G(x,\xi)-\nabla f(x)\right\|^2\mid x\right]\le V_{x_0}.\] Neither the neighborhoods nor their variance bounds are required to be uniform over \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Around every state, oracle noise has a finite uniform second-moment bound, although no single bound need hold globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x_0\in D\;\exists U_{x_0},V_{x_0}<\infty\) with \(\sup_{x\in U_{x_0}}\mathbb{E}[\|G(x,\xi)-\nabla f(x)\|^2\mid x]\le V_{x_0}\).

notation.meaning: neighborhood on which variance is controlled

abla f(x)ight\|^2\mid xight]\le ho\left\|

abla f(x)=0\), the inequality forces \(G(x,\xi)=0\) almost surely; hence this model excludes a nonzero variance floor at stationary points.

knowledge_statements.title: Expected-Smoothness Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected smoothness relative to a common minimizer, allowing residual noise there.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\mathbb{E}_{\xi}[f_{\xi}(x)]\), where the component functions are differentiable, and let \(x_\star\in\operatorname*{argmin} f\). The family satisfies expected smoothness with constant \(L_{\mathrm{ES}}>0\) at \(x_\star\) if, for every admissible \(x\), \[\mathbb{E}_{\xi}\!\left[\left\|
abla f_{\xi}(x)-
abla f_{\xi}(x_\star)ight\|^2ight]\le 2L_{\mathrm{ES}} igl(f(x)-f(x_\star) igr).\] This condition controls stochastic-gradient increments in mean square by objective suboptimality and does not itself require \(
abla f_{\xi}(x_\star)=0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mean-square component-gradient changes from an optimum are controlled by the objective gap, while residual component gradients at the optimum may remain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}_{\xi}[\|\nabla f_{\xi}(x)-\nabla f_{\xi}(x_\star)\|^2]\le2L_{\mathrm{ES}}(f(x)-f(x_\star))\) for all admissible \(x\).

children.title: Variance–Smoothness Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural comparisons between relative-noise and expected-regularity controls.

knowledge_statements.title: Variance–Smoothness Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected smoothness yields an objective-gap-dependent stochastic-gradient variance bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the expected-smoothness inequality holds at a minimizer \(x_\star\) with constant \(L_{\mathrm{ES}}\), and define \(G(x,\xi)=\nabla f_{\xi}(x)\) and \(\sigma_\star^2=\mathbb{E}\|G(x_\star,\xi)\|^2<\infty\). Then, for every admissible \(x\), \[\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\|G(x,\xi)-\nabla f(x)\right\|^2\right]\le 4L_{\mathrm{ES}}\bigl(f(x)-f(x_\star)\bigr)+2\sigma_\star^2.\] Under exact interpolation, \(\sigma_\star^2=0\), so expected smoothness supplies a variance-growth model whose bound vanishes with the objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected smoothness converts component-gradient regularity into a variance bound comprising an objective-gap term and residual variance at an optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[\|G(x,\xi)-\nabla f(x)\|^2]\le4L_{\mathrm{ES}}(f(x)-f(x_\star))+2\sigma_\star^2\).

notation.meaning: second moment of the sample gradient at the reference optimum

children.title: Interpolation Noise-Decay Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes in which stochastic-gradient dispersion contracts near the solution set.

children.title: Exact Interpolation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Finite-data geometries where component objectives share target solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Interpolation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-minimizer regime for differentiable finite-sum or expectation objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\mathbb{E}_{\xi}[f_{\xi}(x)]\) with differentiable component losses. The model is in an exact interpolation regime if there exists \(x_\star\) such that \[x_\star\in\operatorname*{argmin} f_{\xi}\quad\text{for almost every }\xi.\] For unconstrained differentiable components, this implies \(\nabla f_{\xi}(x_\star)=0\) almost surely. Consequently the stochastic-gradient oracle \(G(x,\xi)=\nabla f_{\xi}(x)\) has zero noise and zero second moment at \(x_\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All sampled losses share a common minimizer, so every sampled gradient and the stochastic-gradient noise vanish there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x_\star\;\forall\xi\text{ almost surely},\ x_\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}f_\xi\), hence \(\nabla f_\xi(x_\star)=0\) almost surely.

children.title: Vanishing-Noise Regimes
children.top_down_role: Stochastic-gradient dispersion that contracts near the solution set.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Noise Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic disappearance of stochastic-gradient variance near the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin} f\neq\varnothing\), let \(G(x,\xi)\) be conditionally unbiased, and define \(v(x)=\mathbb{E}[\|G(x,\xi)-\nabla f(x)\|^2\mid x]\). The oracle is in a vanishing-noise regime at \(S\) if \[\lim_{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\to0}v(x)=0.\] Equivalently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists \(\delta>0\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)<\delta\) implies \(v(x)<\varepsilon\). This permits nonzero noise away from the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conditional variance of stochastic-gradient noise tends to zero whenever the iterate approaches the solution set.
assumptions_latex: \(G(x,\xi)\) is conditionally unbiased and square-integrable near \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\to0}\mathbb{E}[\|G(x,\xi)-\nabla f(x)\|^2\mid x]=0\).

children.top_down_role: Residual component mismatch producing small terminal dispersion.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}_{\xi}[\|\nabla f_{\xi}(x_\star)\|^2]\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{int}}^2\); when \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{int}}=0\), \(x_\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}f_\xi\) almost surely.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate interpolation for differentiable convex component objectives, quantified by a residual sample-gradient second moment.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\mathbb{E}_{\xi}[f_{\xi}(x)]\), where every \(f_{\xi}:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable and convex, and choose \(x_\star\in\operatorname*{argmin} f\). A near-interpolation regime with residual level \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{int}}\ge0\) satisfies \[\mathbb{E}_{\xi}\!\left[\left\|\nabla f_{\xi}(x_\star)\right\|^2\right]\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{int}}^2.\] The regime is genuinely approximate when \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{int}}>0\). When \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{int}}=0\), one has \(\nabla f_{\xi}(x_\star)=0\) almost surely, and convexity then gives \(x_\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}f_{\xi}\) almost surely, recovering exact interpolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a population minimizer, the component gradients have a small residual second moment. For differentiable convex components, zero residual recovers a common component minimizer.

children.title: Bounded-Support Noise
children.top_down_role: Noise confined to a uniformly bounded range.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Support Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure norm bound on centered stochastic-oracle noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G(x,\xi)\in\mathbb{R}^d\) be a conditionally unbiased oracle and set \(Z_x=G(x,\xi)-\nabla f(x)\). Its noise has uniformly bounded support if a finite \(B\ge0\) exists such that, for every admissible \(x\), \[\mathbb{P}\!\left(\left\|Z_x\right\|\le B\mid x\right)=1.\] A state-dependent bounded-support model replaces \(B\) by a deterministic finite function \(B(x)\). The uniform condition implies conditional moments of every positive order are finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Centered oracle noise lies almost surely in a fixed norm ball, uniformly over all admissible states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{P}(\|G(x,\xi)-\nabla f(x)\|\le B\mid x)=1\) for every admissible \(x\).

notation.meaning: centered oracle noise at state x

children.title: Sub-Gaussian Noise
children.top_down_role: Light-tailed noise supporting Gaussian-type concentration behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Sub-Gaussian Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional conditional sub-Gaussianity of centered vector oracle noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_x=G(x,\xi)-\mathbb{E}[G(x,\xi)\mid x]\in\mathbb{R}^d\). The oracle noise is conditionally \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian if, for every admissible \(x\), every unit vector \(u\in\mathbb{R}^d\), and every \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}\), \[\mathbb{E}\!\left[\exp\!\left(\lambda\langle u,Z_x\rangle\right)\mid x\right]\le\exp\!\left(\frac{\lambda^2\sigma^2}{2}\right).\] This directional definition supplies Gaussian-type tails for every one-dimensional projection; it does not assert that the coordinates are independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every directional projection of centered oracle noise has a conditional moment-generating function bounded by that of a centered Gaussian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[\exp(\lambda\langle u,Z_x\rangle)\mid x]\le\exp(\lambda^2\sigma^2/2)\) for all admissible \(x\), unit \(u\), and \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}\).

children.title: Sub-Exponential Noise
children.top_down_role: Light-tailed noise with exponential-scale deviation behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Sub-Exponential Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional conditional Bernstein-type control of centered vector oracle noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_x=G(x,\xi)-\mathbb{E}[G(x,\xi)\mid x]\in\mathbb{R}^d\). The oracle noise is conditionally sub-exponential with parameters \((\nu,b)\) if, for every admissible \(x\), every unit vector \(u\), and every \(\lambda\) satisfying \(|\lambda|<1/b\), \[\mathbb{E}\!\left[\exp\!\left(\lambda\langle u,Z_x\rangle\right)\mid x\right]\le\exp\!\left(\frac{\lambda^2\nu^2}{2}\right).\] The parameters control the quadratic and linear regimes of the resulting Bernstein-type directional tail bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every directional noise projection obeys a conditional Bernstein moment-generating-function bound with variance scale and tail scale parameters.
assumptions_latex: \(\nu>0\) and \(b>0\) are uniform over admissible states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[\exp(\lambda\langle u,Z_x\rangle)\mid x]\le\exp(\lambda^2\nu^2/2)\) whenever \(\|u\|_2=1\) and \(|\lambda|<1/b\).

children.title: Heavy-Tail Infinite-Variance Regimes

children.title: Finite-Moment Heavy Tails
children.top_down_role: Heavy-tailed noise controlled through moments below the classical variance scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Moment Heavy Tails
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Heavy-tailed oracle noise with a finite low-order moment but no finite variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_x=G(x,\xi)-\mathbb{E}[G(x,\xi)\mid x]\in\mathbb{R}^d\). A finite-moment infinite-variance regime of order \(p\in(1,2)\) satisfies, for every admissible \(x\), \[\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\|Z_x\right\|^p\mid x\right]\le M_p^p<\infty,\] while \(\mathbb{E}[\|Z_x\|^2\mid x]=\infty\) for at least one relevant state, or uniformly throughout the modeled region. Thus the oracle mean exists, but variance-based SGD assumptions and concentration arguments are unavailable without robustification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Centered oracle noise has a finite moment of order between one and two, while its second moment is infinite in the modeled regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[\|Z_x\|^p\mid x]\le M_p^p<\infty\), with \(\mathbb{E}[\|Z_x\|^2\mid x]=\infty\) at a relevant state or throughout the modeled region.

children.title: Infinite-Variance Noise
children.top_down_role: Noise distributions lacking finite second moments.

knowledge_statements.title: Infinite-Variance Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines conditionally unbiased oracle noise whose second moment does not exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an oracle return \(G(x,\xi)\in\mathbb{R}^d\) at \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\), and define its noise by \(\varepsilon(x,\xi)=G(x,\xi)-\nabla f(x)\). The oracle has infinite-variance noise at \(x\) when \(\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon(x,\xi)\mid x]=0\) and \(\mathbb{E}[\|\varepsilon(x,\xi)\|_2^2\mid x]=+\infty\). It is an infinite-variance noise regime on \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) when this condition holds for every \(x\in D\), although a lower moment \(\mathbb{E}[\|\varepsilon(x,\xi)\|_2^q\mid x]\) may be finite for some \(q\in(1,2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infinite-variance oracle noise is mean-zero conditional error with divergent conditional second moment, possibly retaining a finite moment of order strictly between one and two.
assumptions_latex: \(G(x,\xi)\) and \(\nabla f(x)\) are finite almost surely.
\(\mathbb{E}[\|\varepsilon(x,\xi)\|_2\mid x]<\infty\), so conditional unbiasedness is defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[\|\varepsilon(x,\xi)\|_2^2\mid x]=+\infty\).

notation.meaning: oracle error relative to the true gradient

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation or inspectable locator supports defining infinite-variance noise as necessarily conditionally unbiased; infinite variance alone does not imply mean zero. A source is needed to establish the intended oracle-noise convention and lower-moment qualification.

children.title: Robust Oracle Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Robust stochastic information processing for extreme observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Oracle Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-free geometric-median aggregation of independent oracle replicas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_t\in\mathbb{R}^d\), batch size \(m\geq 1\), step size \(\eta_t>0\), and independent oracle samples \(G_{t,j}=G(x_t,\xi_{t,j})\), choose any geometric median \(\widehat g_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\mathbb{R}^d}\sum_{j=1}^m\|u-G_{t,j}\|_2\). Perform the update \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_t\widehat g_t\). Starting from \(x_0\), repeat until a prescribed iteration budget \(T\), and output \(x_T\) or a specified average of the iterates. The aggregation rule remains defined without finite second moments whenever the sampled oracle values are finite almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iterate, aggregate independent oracle replicas by a geometric median, use the aggregate as the search direction, and return the terminal or prescribed averaged iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_t\widehat g_t\), where \(\widehat g_t\) minimizes the total Euclidean distance to the oracle replicas.

notation.meaning: number of oracle replicas per iteration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The geometric-median rule is well formed and algorithm is an appropriate kind, but no source supports this particular robust-oracle algorithm, its conditional-independence setup, or its asserted applicability without finite second moments.

children.title: Clipping Regimes
children.top_down_role: Tail-control settings based on bounded oracle outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Clipping Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm clipping with fixed or iteration-dependent thresholds for heavy-tailed stochastic gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For thresholds \(\tau_t\in(0,+\infty]\), define \(\operatorname{clip}_{\tau_t}(g)=g\min\{1,\tau_t/\|g\|_2\}\) for \(g\neq 0\), and \(\operatorname{clip}_{\tau_t}(0)=0\). Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^d\), step sizes \(\eta_t>0\), and oracle samples \(G_t=G(x_t,\xi_t)\), set \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_t\operatorname{clip}_{\tau_t}(G_t)\). Fixed-threshold clipping has \(\tau_t=\tau<\infty\); growing-threshold clipping has finite \(\tau_t\) with \(\tau_t\to\infty\); and the unclipped regime has \(\tau_t=+infty\). After \(T\) iterations, output \(x_T\) or a prescribed iterate average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip each stochastic gradient to a threshold before updating; fixed, growing, and infinite thresholds respectively define fixed-clipping, vanishing-clipping-bias, and unclipped regimes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\operatorname{clip}_{\tau_t}(G_t)\|_2\leq\tau_t\) whenever \(\tau_t<+\infty\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the clipping taxonomy. The unclipped threshold contains the typo \(+infty\) instead of \(+\infty\), and the plain statement calls growing thresholds a vanishing-clipping-bias regime although the LaTeX statement supplies no conditions ensuring that bias vanishes.

children.title: Sampling Designs
children.top_down_role: Data and component selection mechanisms determining estimator dependence, variance, and cost.

children.title: Independent Sampling with Replacement
children.top_down_role: Independent population or component sampling.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Sampling with Replacement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent component sampling for finite-sum stochastic-gradient updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). Independent sampling with replacement draws indices \(I_0,I_1,\ldots\) independently from a fixed distribution \(p\) on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), allowing an index to recur at any two draws. Under uniform sampling, \(p_i=1/n\), and the component gradient \(G_t=\nabla f_{I_t}(x_t)\) satisfies \(\mathbb{E}[G_t\mid x_t]=\nabla f(x_t)\). A basic SGD realization initializes \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^d\), updates \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_tG_t\), and returns \(x_T\) or a prescribed average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each component index is drawn independently and may reappear. Uniform draws make the sampled component gradient conditionally unbiased for the finite-sum gradient.
assumptions_latex: \(I_t\) is independent of earlier draws and satisfies \(\mathbb{P}(I_t=i)=1/n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[\nabla f_{I_t}(x_t)\mid x_t]=\nabla f(x_t)\).

children.title: Without-Replacement Sampling Family
children.top_down_role: Epoch-based dependent sampling from finite populations.

children.title: Random Reshuffling
children.top_down_role: Epoch-wise sampling through fresh random permutations.

knowledge_statements.title: Random Reshuffling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One fresh random permutation per finite-sum epoch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), initialize \(x_{0,0}\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At epoch \(s\), sample a permutation \(\pi_s\) uniformly from all permutations of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), set \(x_{s,0}=x_{s-1,n}\) when \(s>0\), and for \(k=0,\ldots,n-1\) update \(x_{s,k+1}=x_{s,k}-\eta_{s,k}\nabla f_{\pi_s(k+1)}(x_{s,k})\). After \(S\) epochs, output \(x_{S,n}\) or a prescribed average. Each component is used exactly once per epoch, while permutations are sampled independently across epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random reshuffling draws a fresh permutation each epoch and processes every component exactly once in that permutation order.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi_s\) is uniform and independent of permutations from earlier epochs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{s,n}\) is obtained after exactly one update from every component in the order \(\pi_s\).

notation.meaning: random permutation used during epoch s
iterate after k component updates in epoch s

source_refs.source_title: First-Order Methods in Optimization
source_refs.locator: 8.4 The Incremental Projected Subgradient Method p. 229

review_flags: locator may cover incremental ordering more generally than random reshuffling
