children.title: Bias-Induced Error Floors
children.top_down_role: Terminal accuracy limits caused by persistent oracle bias.

knowledge_statements.title: Bias-Induced Error Floors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact error floor for a strongly convex quadratic with constant oracle bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac{\mu}{2}\|x\|^2\) on \(\mathbb{R}^d\), where \(\mu>0\), and let the oracle return \(g(x)=\nabla f(x)+b=\mu x+b\) for a fixed \(b\ne0\). With the update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_k g(x_k)\), gains satisfying \(0<\mu\alpha_k<1\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\alpha_k\to0\) yield \(x_k\to-b/\mu\). Since the true minimizer is \(x^*=0\), the limiting distance and objective gap are \[\|x_k-x^*\|\to\frac{\|b\|}{\mu},\qquad f(x_k)-f(x^*)\to\frac{\|b\|^2}{2\mu}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant biased gradient on a quadratic converges to a displaced point, leaving exact nonzero distance and objective error floors.

notation.meaning: True minimizer of the unbiased objective.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic calculation and error-floor values are correct and the counterexample kind fits the leaf, but the record supplies no source citation.

children.title: Bias-Floor Scaling
children.top_down_role: Dependence of terminal error on bias magnitude, gain, or geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Bias-Floor Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-convexity scaling of displacement caused by bounded persistent bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, \(\mu\)-strongly convex, and \(L\)-smooth, with minimizer \(x^*\). Suppose a limiting point \(x_b\) of the biased mean dynamics satisfies \(\nabla f(x_b)+b=0\) for a constant bias with \(\|b\|\le\varepsilon_b\). Strong monotonicity of \(\nabla f\) gives \[\|x_b-x^*\|\le\frac{\varepsilon_b}{\mu}.\] Smoothness then gives \[f(x_b)-f(x^*)\le\frac{L\varepsilon_b^2}{2\mu^2}.\] The distance dependence \(\varepsilon_b/\mu\) and quadratic objective dependence are attained, up to the displayed constants, by strongly convex quadratic objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strong convexity, a bias of size ε causes at most order ε/μ distance error and order ε² objective error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_b-x^*\|\le\varepsilon_b/\mu\) and \(f(x_b)-f(x^*)\le L\varepsilon_b^2/(2\mu^2)\).

notation.meaning: Stationary point of the biased mean field.
Upper bound on the bias norm.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distance and objective-gap bounds are mathematically consistent under the stated strong-convexity and smoothness assumptions, but this nontrivial scaling property has no source citation.

children.title: Misspecified Limit Points
children.top_down_role: Convergence toward equilibria associated with biased mean dynamics.

knowledge_statements.title: Misspecified Limit Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A persistent additive oracle bias shifts the stochastic-approximation limit away from the true minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^2/2\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), whose unique minimizer is \(x^\star=0\). Consider the biased oracle \(G(x)=x+b\), where \(b\ne0\), and the recursion \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_kG(x_k)\). If \(0<\alpha_k<1\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\alpha_k\to0\), then \(x_k+b=(x_0+b)\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-\alpha_j)\to0\). Consequently, \(x_k\to-b\ne x^\star\), so the algorithm converges to the zero of the misspecified mean oracle rather than to the minimizer of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a quadratic objective, a fixed additive gradient bias makes stochastic approximation converge to the shifted point minus the bias, not to the true minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to-b\ne0=x^\star\).
review_flags: Exact elementary counterexample supplied, but no locator hint directly supports persistent-bias limit displacement.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elementary biased-quadratic counterexample is mathematically coherent, and counterexample fits the leaf. A specific authoritative locator supporting persistent-bias limit displacement is required.

children.title: Extreme-Observation Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Breakdown of variance-based analysis and standard concentration under extreme observations.

children.title: Heavy-Tail Failures
children.top_down_role: Breakdown of variance-based guarantees under slowly decaying noise tails.

knowledge_statements.title: Heavy-Tail Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-variance and root-sample concentration conclusions fail for stable heavy-tailed gradient noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^2/2\) and let the stochastic oracle be \(G(x,\xi)=x+\xi\), where \(\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots\) are independent symmetric \(p\)-stable variables with \(1<p<2\), location zero, and nonzero scale. Then \(\mathbb{E}[G(x,\xi)]=x\), but \(\mathbb{E}[\xi^2]=\infty\). Stability gives \(n^{-1/p}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i\) the same distributional type as \(\xi_1\); hence the sample-mean error scales as \(n^{1/p-1}\), not \(n^{-1/2}\). Variance-based SGD guarantees and sub-Gaussian gradient-concentration bounds therefore do not apply under this oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbiased stable heavy-tailed oracle can have infinite variance, with sample averages converging more slowly than the usual square-root rate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[\xi^2]=\infty\) and the sample-mean noise has scale \(n^{1/p-1}\), rather than \(n^{-1/2}\).

notation.meaning: Stability index of the heavy-tailed noise

review_flags: The stable-law construction is standard, but the supplied locators do not cover heavy-tailed stochastic approximation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The p-stable construction and stated sample-mean scale are plausible and fit a heavy-tail failure boundary, but no cited source supports the stable-law facts or their applicability boundary.

children.title: Outlier Failures
children.top_down_role: Instability or distortion caused by rare extreme observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Outlier Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rare, unbounded oracle observations preclude uniform mean-square stability without magnitude or moment control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\equiv0\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), initialize \(x_0=0\), and take one stochastic-gradient step \(x_1=x_0-\eta G\) with \(\eta>0\). For arbitrary \(M>0\), let \(G=M\) with probability \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) and \(G=0\) otherwise. Then \(\mathbb{E}|x_1-x_0|^2=\eta^2\varepsilon M^2\). Because this quantity is unbounded as \(M\to\infty\) while the outlier probability remains fixed, no uniform mean-square displacement or stability bound can depend only on \(\eta\) and \(\varepsilon\); an outlier-magnitude, moment, clipping, or robust-aggregation assumption is necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a fixed small outlier probability permits arbitrarily large mean-square SGD displacement when outlier magnitudes are unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{M>0}\mathbb{E}|x_1-x_0|^2=\infty\).

notation.meaning: Probability of an outlying oracle value

review_flags: Exact one-step construction is elementary, but no supplied source locator addresses contamination or outliers.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-step calculation is correct and counterexample is appropriate for the leaf. A source with a specific locator on unrestricted outliers or contamination is missing.

children.title: Concentration Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Loss of standard deviation-control or high-probability behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Concentration Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential concentration is unavailable when gradient noise lacks the moments implied by such tail bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\ge1\) satisfy \(\mathbb{P}(Y>t)=t^{-p}\) for \(t\ge1\), where \(1<p<2\), and define \(\xi=Y-\mathbb{E}Y\). For independent copies \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\), the average \(\bar\xi_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i\) has infinite second moment. Therefore there is no constant \(c>0\) for which \(\mathbb{P}(|\bar\xi_n|\ge t)\le2\exp(-cn t^2)\) holds for every \(n\ge1\) and \(t>0\), since such a tail inequality would imply a finite second moment. Thus unbiasedness and a finite first moment alone do not yield sub-Gaussian concentration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Centered Pareto noise has a finite mean but infinite variance, so its sample average cannot satisfy a uniform sub-Gaussian concentration inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No \(c>0\) yields \(\mathbb{P}(|\bar\xi_n|\ge t)\le2e^{-cnt^2}\) uniformly over \(n\ge1\) and \(t>0\).
review_flags: The moment-versus-tail implication is standard, but the available source hints do not cover heavy-tail concentration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The centered Pareto example correctly exposes failure of a uniform sub-Gaussian bound and fits the failure-boundary container, but it has no supporting citation.

children.title: Robustification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Noise regimes requiring clipping, truncation, aggregation, or robust estimation.

knowledge_statements.title: Robustification Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clipping controls influence only by accepting bias when valid gradients exceed the clipping threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau>0\), define scalar clipping by \(T_\tau(g)=\operatorname{sign}(g)\min\{|g|,\tau\}\). This transformation satisfies \(|T_\tau(g)|\le\tau\), so a single observation has bounded influence. However, for a deterministic valid oracle value \(g\) with \(|g|>\tau\), its clipping bias is \(|T_\tau(g)-g|=|g|-\tau>0\). Hence no fixed finite threshold simultaneously bounds every observation and remains unbiased for all unrestricted valid gradient distributions. A useful clipping guarantee must therefore impose a gradient-scale or tail condition, or explicitly retain a threshold-dependent bias term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite clipping bounds outlier influence but necessarily biases valid gradients exceeding the threshold; guarantees need scale assumptions or an explicit bias term.
assumptions_latex: Valid gradient magnitudes are not assumed bounded by \(\tau\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|g|>\tau\) implies \(|T_\tau(g)-g|=|g|-\tau>0\).

notation.meaning: Scalar clipping operator at threshold tau

review_flags: The clipping boundary is explicit, but none of the supplied locators directly supports robustification tradeoffs.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clipping identity is correct and the content kind fits. The broader robustification claim needs a located source, and “bounded influence” should be interpreted or defined precisely by that source.

children.title: Temporal-Dependence Failure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Bias or instability induced by correlated samples, slow mixing, or obsolete information.

children.title: Dependent-Sample Failures
children.top_down_role: Bias or variance distortion caused by correlated oracle samples.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependent-Sample Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal oracle unbiasedness does not ensure convergence when temporal dependence preserves a permanent sample shock.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^2/2\), choose a Rademacher variable \(Z\), and set \(Z_k=Z\) for every \(k\). The oracle \(G_k(x)=x+Z_k\) is marginally unbiased because \(\mathbb{E}[G_k(x)]=x\). Nevertheless, the recursion \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_kG_k(x_k)\), with \(0<\alpha_k<1\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), satisfies \(x_k+Z=(x_0+Z)\prod_{j<k}(1-\alpha_j)\to0\). Thus \(x_k\to-Z\) almost surely rather than to the minimizer \(0\). Conditional martingale-difference or adequate-mixing assumptions cannot be replaced by marginal unbiasedness alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfectly dependent noise may be unbiased at every time marginally yet make stochastic approximation converge almost surely to a random incorrect point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to-Z\ne0\) almost surely.
review_flags: Exact dependence counterexample supplied, but the candidate source inventory lacks a temporal-dependence theorem or example.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The perfectly dependent Rademacher construction is internally correct and counterexample fits the leaf. A specific source on conditional unbiasedness, martingale differences, or dependent-sample failure is required.

children.title: Poor-Mixing Failures
children.top_down_role: Slow decorrelation regimes that invalidate nominal stochastic approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Poor-Mixing Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slow Markov mixing inflates sampling error and destroys constants uniform over dependence strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((Z_k)\) be the stationary Markov chain on \(\{-1,1\}\) that switches sign with probability \(\delta\in(0,1/2]\) at each step. Then \(\mathbb{E}Z_k=0\) and \(\operatorname{Cov}(Z_0,Z_h)=(1-2\delta)^h\). For \(\bar Z_n=n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^n Z_k\), 
\[\operatorname{Var}(\bar Z_n)=\frac{1}{n^2}\left(n+2\sum_{h=1}^{n-1}(n-h)(1-2\delta)^h\right).\]
When \(n\delta\) is large, this variance is of order \((n\delta)^{-1}\), rather than uniformly of order \(n^{-1}\). Consequently, IID-rate stochastic-gradient guarantees cannot hold uniformly as the mixing rate \(\delta\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slowly switching two-state Markov chain reduces the effective sample size from order n to order n times its switching probability.
assumptions_latex: The chain switches sign independently with probability \(\delta\) per transition
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Var}(\bar Z_n)=\Theta((n\delta)^{-1})\) when \(n\delta\) is sufficiently large.

notation.meaning: Empirical average of the Markov samples

review_flags: The covariance computation is explicit, but the supplied mixing-matrix locator does not directly certify Markov-sample mixing rates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The covariance formula is coherent and the failure-boundary role fits, but the stated Theta regime and resulting nonuniform IID-rate conclusion require a directly supporting locator.

children.title: Staleness Failures
children.top_down_role: Instability or bias caused by obsolete state or gradient information.

knowledge_statements.title: Staleness Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Delayed gradients shrink the stable stepsize range even for a scalar strongly convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=x^2/2\), delayed gradient descent with fixed delay \(d\in\mathbb{N}_0\) obeys \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta x_{k-d}\), given an initial history \(x_{-d},\ldots,x_0\). Its characteristic equation is \(r^{d+1}-r^d+\eta=0\). Asymptotic stability holds precisely for \(0<\eta<2\sin\!\bigl(\pi/(4d+2)\bigr)\). At the boundary a characteristic root lies on the unit circle, and above it some initial histories fail to converge to zero. Thus a stepsize stable without delay can become unstable when gradients are sufficiently stale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a scalar quadratic, delay reduces the exact stable stepsize threshold; crossing it produces nonconvergent trajectories for some initial histories.
assumptions_latex: The update uses the exact gradient delayed by \(d\) iterations
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Asymptotic stability is equivalent to \(0<\eta<2\sin\!\bigl(\pi/(4d+2)\bigr)\).
review_flags: The exact delay-stability threshold requires direct source certification; supplied locators do not address delayed recursions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recurrence and characteristic equation are consistent, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. The exact necessary-and-sufficient delay-stability threshold requires authoritative source certification.

children.title: Temporal-Mismatch Effects
children.top_down_role: Combined consequences of dependence, slow mixing, and delayed information.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal-Mismatch Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A delayed oracle for a drifting objective carries a bias proportional to cumulative target motion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_k(x)=	frac12(x-m_k)^2\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), and suppose iteration \(k\) uses the delayed gradient \(G_k(x)=
abla f_{k-d}(x)=x-m_{k-d}\), where \(d\ge1\). Relative to the current gradient, the temporal-mismatch error is 
\[G_k(x)-
abla f_k(x)=m_k-m_{k-d}.\]
If \(|m_{j+1}-m_j|\le v\) for every \(j\), then \(|G_k(x)-
abla f_k(x)|\le dv\). This bound is attained by the linear drift \(m_j=jv\), so delay and drift can create an irreducible oracle discrepancy of order \(dv\), even when every delayed gradient is evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a drifting quadratic target, a delay of d steps creates gradient error at most d times the per-step drift, and linear drift attains it.
assumptions_latex: The oracle returns the exact gradient of the delayed objective
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|G_k(x)-\nabla f_k(x)|\le dv\), with equality possible under linear drift.
review_flags: The mismatch identity is elementary, but no supplied locator addresses nonstationary delayed objectives.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mismatch identity and dv bound are elementary, and property is a reasonable role for an effects leaf. A supporting locator is absent; the intended domain should also state v≥0 and k≥d.

children.title: Ambiguous Limit-Set Dynamics
children.top_down_role: Limit-set ambiguity when equilibrium geometry does not select a unique stable point.

children.title: Nonisolated Limit Sets
children.top_down_role: Continuum-valued or set-valued asymptotic destinations.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonisolated Limit Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A continuum of minimizers permits initialization-dependent limits despite exact smooth gradient descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x,y)=x^2/2\) on \(\mathbb{R}^2\). Its minimizer set is the nonisolated line \(S=\{(0,y):y\in\mathbb{R}\}\). Gradient descent with constant \(0<\eta<2\) satisfies \(x_{k+1}=(1-\eta)x_k\) and \(y_{k+1}=y_k\). Therefore \((x_k,y_k)\to(0,y_0)\). Every initialization converges to a minimizer, but the objective and update do not select a unique point of \(S\); the limiting point retains the initial component tangent to the minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient descent on a quadratic flat in one direction converges to a continuum of possible minimizers selected by the initial flat-direction coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_k,y_k)\to(0,y_0)\in S\), so the selected limit depends on initialization.
review_flags: Explicit smooth counterexample supplied, but the source hints do not directly discuss nonisolated stochastic-approximation limits.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The flat-direction quadratic counterexample is correct and matches nonisolated limit selection, but no source with a specific locator is cited.

children.title: Competing Attractors
children.top_down_role: Multiple stable destinations with initialization-sensitive or noise-sensitive selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Competing Attractors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonconvex objective can have distinct attracting minimizers whose basins are separated by an unstable stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=(x^2-1)^2/4\), so \(f'(x)=x(x^2-1)\), and apply gradient descent \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta f'(x_k)\). If \(0<\eta\le1/2\) and \(0<x_0<1\), then \(x_k\to1\); if \(-1<x_0<0\), then \(x_k\to-1\). The initial point \(x_0=0\) remains at the unstable stationary point. Thus the two strict minimizers \(-1\) and \(1\) are competing attractors, and arbitrarily close initial conditions on opposite sides of zero have different limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a double-well objective, gradient descent approaches either minimizer according to the initial sign, while zero separates the two attraction basins.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_0>0\Rightarrow x_k\to1\), \(x_0<0\Rightarrow x_k\to-1\), and \(x_0=0\Rightarrow x_k=0\).
review_flags: The basin construction is explicit, but no supplied source locator directly treats competing nonconvex attractors.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The double-well construction is consistent with the stated initialization and stepsize ranges, and counterexample fits competing attractors. Direct source support is missing.

children.title: Persistent Cycling
children.top_down_role: Recurrent asymptotic motion that prevents point convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A skew mean field can produce bounded, perpetually rotating stochastic-approximation iterates under standard diminishing stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\), choose \(z_0\in\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}\), and consider \(z_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_kJz_k\) with \(\alpha_k=1/(k+1)\). Identifying \(\mathbb{R}^2\) with \(\mathbb{C}\), the update is \(z_{k+1}=(1+i\alpha_k)z_k\). Since \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), the radii satisfy \(\lVert z_k\rVert\to r_\infty>0\); since \(\sum_k\arctan(\alpha_k)=\infty\), the accumulated angle is unbounded. Hence the bounded iterates rotate indefinitely and do not converge, despite \(\alpha_k\to0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=
\infty\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a purely rotational mean field, standard diminishing stepsizes produce bounded iterates of positive limiting radius that rotate forever and never converge.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is the planar skew-symmetric rotation matrix
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert z_k\rVert\to r_\infty>0\) while \((z_k)\) does not converge.
review_flags: The rotational recursion is explicit, but the available textbook locators do not directly support persistent cycling in stochastic approximation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rotational recursion supports the stated bounded nonconvergence phenomenon, and counterexample fits persistent cycling in general stochastic approximation. A located source is required, particularly to establish its intended scope within the SA-SGD method family.

children.title: Limit-Selection Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Failure of equilibrium geometry to determine a unique limiting outcome.

knowledge_statements.title: Limit-Selection Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines ambiguity among multiple attainable components of a stochastic approximation limit set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X_k)_{k\geq 0}\) be a stochastic approximation process in a metric space, and suppose its limit \(X_\infty\) exists almost surely in a closed set \(L\). Limit-selection ambiguity holds when there are disjoint measurable components \(L_1,L_2\subseteq L\) such that \(\mathbb P(X_\infty\in L_1)>0\) and \(\mathbb P(X_\infty\in L_2)>0\). Thus the algorithm and initialization determine only the admissible limit set, while the realized noise path selects among at least two distinct components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Limit-selection ambiguity means that identical algorithmic data can lead, with positive probability, to two different components of the admissible limit set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(X_\infty\in L_1)>0\) and \(\mathbb P(X_\infty\in L_2)>0\).

notation.meaning: Distinct measurable components of the limit set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No evidence is supplied for this proposed stochastic-approximation definition, and the record calls arbitrary disjoint measurable subsets “components.” A source is needed to determine the intended limit-set notion and hypotheses.

children.title: Constant-Gain Stationary Error Regimes
children.top_down_role: Persistent fluctuations and steady-state bias replacing exact convergence.

children.title: Constant-Gain Noise Floors
children.top_down_role: Persistent fluctuation levels under nonvanishing gain.

knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Gain Noise Floors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stationary error floor for scalar constant-gain SGD on a strongly convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\lambda x^2/2\), consider \(X_{k+1}=(1-\alpha\lambda)X_k-\alpha\xi_{k+1}\), where \((\xi_k)_{k\geq1}\) are independent and identically distributed, centered, and have variance \(\sigma^2\). If \(0<\alpha\lambda<2\), the recursion has a unique invariant distribution \(\pi\) with mean zero and variance \[\operatorname{Var}_\pi(X)=\frac{\alpha^2\sigma^2}{1-(1-\alpha\lambda)^2}=\frac{\alpha\sigma^2}{\lambda(2-\alpha\lambda)}.\] Consequently, \(\mathbb E_\pi[f(X)-f(0)]=\alpha\sigma^2/[2(2-\alpha\lambda)]>0\), so a fixed positive gain has a nonzero stationary mean-square error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constant-gain SGD on a noisy scalar quadratic has a positive stationary error proportional to the gain rather than concentrating exactly at the minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \((\xi_k)_{k\geq1}\) are independent and identically distributed with \(\mathbb E\xi_k=0\) and \(\mathbb E\xi_k^2=\sigma^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E_\pi[f(X)-f(0)]=\alpha\sigma^2/[2(2-\alpha\lambda)]>0\).

children.title: Stationary Bias
children.top_down_role: Displacement of steady-state behavior from the target solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationary Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes why an invariant mean need not be a stationary point for nonlinear objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(X_{k+1}=X_k-\alpha(
abla f(X_k)+\xi_{k+1})\) with \(\mathbb E[\xi_{k+1}\mid X_k]=0\), and let \(\pi\) be an invariant distribution having the required first moments. Stationarity implies \[\int 
abla f(x)\,\pi(dx)=0.\] In general this identity does not imply \(
abla f( ar x)=0\) for \( ar x=\int x\,\pi(dx)\), because nonlinear gradients need not commute with expectation. Hence the invariant mean may be biased away from every optimizer, even though the stochastic gradient is conditionally unbiased.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbiased stochastic gradient can still yield a biased stationary mean because averaging generally does not commute with a nonlinear gradient.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi\) is invariant and all displayed integrals are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\int\nabla f(x)\,\pi(dx)=0\) need not imply \(\nabla f(\int x\,\pi(dx))=0\).

children.title: Invariant-Distribution Spread
children.top_down_role: Steady-state dispersion across local geometry and noise regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Invariant-Distribution Spread
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lyapunov representation of stationary covariance for linear constant-gain SGD.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}\) be symmetric positive definite and consider \(X_{k+1}=(I-\alpha H)X_k-\alpha\xi_{k+1}\), where \((\xi_k)_{k\geq1}\) are independent and identically distributed with mean zero and covariance \(\Sigma\). If \(\rho(I-\alpha H)<1\), the recursion has a unique invariant distribution with mean zero and covariance \(C\) satisfying \[C=(I-\alpha H)C(I-\alpha H)^{\mathsf T}+\alpha^2\Sigma,\qquad C=\alpha^2\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}(I-\alpha H)^j\Sigma((I-\alpha H)^{\mathsf T})^j.\] Nonzero noise produces nonzero invariant spread in each stable direction excited by \(\Sigma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For linear constant-gain SGD with i.i.d. noise, the invariant covariance solves a discrete Lyapunov equation and is nonzero in noise-excited directions.
assumptions_latex: \((\xi_k)_{k\geq1}\) are independent and identically distributed, centered, and have covariance \(\Sigma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=\alpha^2\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}(I-\alpha H)^j\Sigma((I-\alpha H)^{\mathsf T})^j\).

children.title: Gain–Accuracy Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Balance between responsiveness, stationary variance, and terminal bias.

knowledge_statements.title: Gain–Accuracy Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact speed–accuracy tradeoff for scalar constant-gain stochastic gradient recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the scalar quadratic recursion \(X_{k+1}=(1-\alpha\lambda)X_k-\alpha\xi_{k+1}\), suppose \((\xi_k)_{k\geq1}\) are independent and identically distributed, centered, and have variance \(\sigma^2\), and let \(0<\alpha\lambda<2\). The deterministic contraction factor is \(r=|1-\alpha\lambda|\), whereas the stationary expected objective error is \[\varepsilon_\infty(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sigma^2}{2(2-\alpha\lambda)}.\] As \(\alpha\downarrow0\), one has \(1-r=\alpha\lambda\) for all sufficiently small \(\alpha\), and \(\varepsilon_\infty(\alpha)\sim\alpha\sigma^2/4\). Thus reducing the gain lowers the noise floor linearly while increasing the relaxation scale \((1-r)^{-1}\) proportionally to \(1/\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For scalar quadratic SGD with i.i.d. noise, smaller constant gains reduce stationary error linearly but increase the transient relaxation scale inversely with the gain.
assumptions_latex: \((\xi_k)_{k\geq1}\) are independent and identically distributed, centered, and have variance \(\sigma^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon_\infty(\alpha)\sim\alpha\sigma^2/4\) and \((1-r)^{-1}\sim1/(\alpha\lambda)\) as \(\alpha\downarrow0\).

children.title: Adaptive-Momentum Instability Coupling
children.top_down_role: Instability, nonconvergence, or distorted geometry caused by momentum and adaptive preconditioning.

children.title: Adaptive Scaling Failures
children.top_down_role: Instability or distorted progress caused by data-dependent coordinate scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Scaling Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by vanishing adaptive denominators and uncontrolled coordinatewise effective gains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the coordinatewise update \(x_{k+1,i}=x_{k,i}-\alpha m_{k,i}/(\sqrt{v_{k,i}}+\varepsilon)\), define the effective gain \(a_{k,i}=\alpha/(\sqrt{v_{k,i}}+\varepsilon)\). If \(\varepsilon=0\) and \(v_{k,i}=0\), the update is undefined whenever \(m_{k,i}\neq0\). More generally, if \(v_{k,i}\downarrow0\) while \(|m_{k,i}|\) does not decrease comparably, then \(|a_{k,i}m_{k,i}|\) is unbounded. Consequently bounded raw gradients alone do not ensure bounded adaptive steps without a positive denominator floor or an equivalent gain bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive scaling fails when its second-moment denominator vanishes, making a coordinate update undefined or arbitrarily large despite bounded raw gradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_k|x_{k+1,i}-x_{k,i}|=\infty\), or the update is undefined.

notation.meaning: Momentum or first-moment estimate in coordinate i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elementary denominator failure is plausible and the failure-boundary kind fits, but no adaptive-method source supports the proposed generalization or identifies the intended update family.

children.title: Momentum Failures
children.top_down_role: Oscillation, amplification, or nonconvergence caused by inertial state.

knowledge_statements.title: Momentum Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp scalar stability boundary for the deterministic heavy-ball recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Apply heavy-ball momentum to \(f(x)=\lambda x^2/2\): \[x_{k+1}=(1+\beta-\alpha\lambda)x_k-\beta x_{k-1}.\] For \(0\leq\beta<1\), every trajectory converges to zero exactly when \(0<\alpha\lambda<2(1+\beta)\). If \(\alpha\lambda>2(1+\beta)\), the characteristic polynomial \(z^2-(1+\beta-\alpha\lambda)z+\beta\) has a root outside the closed unit disk, so some initialization diverges geometrically. Equality gives a nondecaying boundary mode and therefore does not ensure convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heavy-ball momentum on a scalar quadratic becomes unstable when the stepsize–curvature product reaches or exceeds twice one plus the momentum coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convergence for every initialization holds iff \(0<\alpha\lambda<2(1+\beta)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated scalar heavy-ball boundary is mathematically plausible and appropriately classified as a failure boundary, but the sharp iff claim has no cited evidence.

children.title: Coupled Adaptive-Momentum Instability
children.top_down_role: Failure regimes created by feedback between moving preconditioners and momentum states.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Adaptive-Momentum Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frozen-mode stability boundary coupling momentum with an adaptive denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a scalar quadratic mode of curvature \(\lambda>0\) with momentum coefficient \(0\leq\beta<1\) and frozen adaptive denominator \(d>0\): \[x_{k+1}=\left(1+\beta-\frac{\alpha\lambda}{d}\right)x_k-\beta x_{k-1}.\] The mode is stable exactly when \(0<\alpha\lambda/d<2(1+\beta)\). Hence decreasing the adaptive denominator below \(\alpha\lambda/[2(1+\beta)]\) moves the coupled adaptive-momentum mode across the unit-circle stability boundary, although either the unscaled stepsize or momentum coefficient may appear benign when considered alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive rescaling can amplify an otherwise acceptable momentum step beyond the heavy-ball stability boundary, creating a coupled instability.
assumptions_latex: The denominator is frozen while the local scalar mode is analyzed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The frozen mode is unstable when \(d\leq\alpha\lambda/[2(1+\beta)]\).
review_flags: frozen-denominator scope must not be generalized to arbitrary time variation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this frozen-denominator model as a coupled adaptive-momentum failure. At equality the mode is nonconvergent rather than necessarily divergent, so a source is also needed to fix the intended meaning of “unstable.”

children.title: Preconditioner Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Ill-conditioned, vanishing, or excessively amplified adaptive scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral failure boundary for preconditioned gradient descent on a quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Hx/2\) with \(H\succ0\), and let a fixed symmetric preconditioner satisfy \(P\succ0\). The update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha PHx_k\) converges for every initialization exactly when \[0<\alpha\lambda_{\max}(P^{1/2}HP^{1/2})<2.\] If \(P=D^{-1}\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(D)\downarrow0\), then \(\lambda_{\max}(P)\uparrow\infty\); without compensating reduction of \(\alpha\), the stability inequality eventually fails. Thus a vanishing scale in \(D\) is a genuine preconditioner degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vanishing preconditioner denominator produces unbounded effective curvature and eventually violates the quadratic stability condition unless the stepsize is reduced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convergence holds iff \(\alpha\lambda_{\max}(P^{1/2}HP^{1/2})<2\); degeneration of \(D\) can violate this bound.

notation.meaning: Scale matrix whose inverse is the preconditioner

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed quadratic spectral condition and degeneracy mechanism are plausible and fit a failure-boundary leaf, but neither the iff condition nor its degeneration consequence has cited support.

children.title: Batch-Parallel Scaling Boundary
children.top_down_role: Loss of statistical or computational benefit from oversized batches and synchronization overhead.

children.title: Mini-Batch Statistical Saturation
children.top_down_role: Batch-size regimes where additional samples yield little variance or accuracy improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Mini-Batch Statistical Saturation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance floor for equicorrelated stochastic gradients within a mini-batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_1,\ldots,G_B\) be scalar unbiased gradient samples with common variance \(\sigma^2\) and pairwise covariance \(\rho\sigma^2\), where \(0\leq\rho\leq1\). For the mini-batch average \(\bar G_B=B^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^B G_i\), \[\operatorname{Var}(\bar G_B)=\frac{\sigma^2}{B}\bigl(1+(B-1)\rho\bigr)=\sigma^2\left(\rho+\frac{1-\rho}{B}\right).\] Therefore \(\operatorname{Var}(\bar G_B)\to\rho\sigma^2\) as \(B\to\infty\). Positive within-batch correlation prevents the usual variance from decreasing below this statistical saturation floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correlated samples make mini-batch variance saturate at a positive floor, so increasing batch size eventually yields negligible statistical improvement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{B\to\infty}\operatorname{Var}(\bar G_B)=\rho\sigma^2\).

children.title: Parallel Scaling Limits
children.top_down_role: Worker-count regimes where speedup becomes sublinear or disappears.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Scaling Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Amdahl-type upper bound for synchronous parallel speedup per optimization iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose one serial optimization iteration takes time \(T_1=T_{\mathrm s}+T_{\mathrm p}\), where \(T_{\mathrm s}>0\) is intrinsically serial and \(T_{\mathrm p}\) is perfectly divisible among \(P\) workers. Then the parallel iteration time satisfies \(T_P\geq T_{\mathrm s}+T_{\mathrm p}/P\), and its speedup obeys \[S_P=\frac{T_1}{T_P}\leq\frac{1}{s+(1-s)/P},\qquad s=\frac{T_{\mathrm s}}{T_1}.\] Consequently \(S_P\leq1/s\) as \(P\to\infty\); any positive serial fraction imposes a finite strong-scaling limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive serial fraction caps synchronous optimization speedup, even when the remaining per-iteration computation parallelizes perfectly.
assumptions_latex: Only \(T_{\mathrm p}\) is perfectly divisible across workers.

notation.meaning: Serial fraction of single-worker iteration time

children.title: Synchronization Overhead
children.top_down_role: Communication and barrier costs that dominate parallel batch execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronization Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock lower bound for a barrier-synchronous distributed stochastic-gradient iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a barrier-synchronous iteration with \(P\) workers, let \(C_i\) be worker \(i\)'s local computation time and let \(T_{\mathrm{sync}}(P)\geq0\) include communication and barrier costs. The iteration time satisfies \[T_P\geq\max_{1\leq i\leq P}C_i+T_{\mathrm{sync}}(P).\] Even if local computation vanishes as \(P\) increases, a nonvanishing synchronization cost gives \(T_P\geq T_{\mathrm{sync}}(P)\), limiting attainable wall-clock speedup.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronous iteration must wait for its slowest worker and complete communication, so nonvanishing barrier cost limits wall-clock scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_P\geq\max_{1\leq i\leq P}C_i+T_{\mathrm{sync}}(P)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Critical Batch-Size Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Crossover boundary for mini-batch SGD under a deterministic-plus-sampling-error convergence bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose mini-batch SGD with batch size \(b\ge 1\) and iteration budget \(T\ge 1\) satisfies
\[
\mathbb{E}[F(\bar x_T)-F^*]\le \frac{A}{T}+\frac{C}{\sqrt{bT}},
\]
where \(A,C>0\) are independent of \(b\) and \(T\). Define the critical batch size by
\[
b_{\mathrm{crit}}(T):=\frac{C^2T}{A^2}.
\]
For \(b<b_{\mathrm{crit}}(T)\), the sampling term exceeds the deterministic term, so increasing \(b\) improves the displayed bound. For \(b>b_{\mathrm{crit}}(T)\), the deterministic term dominates; further batch growth cannot improve the bound below its order \(A/T\) without increasing \(T\) or changing the method. Equality is the crossover regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The critical batch size equates deterministic and sampling errors. Below it, larger batches improve the bound; above it, the deterministic iteration error dominates and batch-parallel gains saturate.
assumptions_latex: The stated convergence bound holds with constants \(A,C>0\) independent of \(b\) and \(T\).
Mini-batch sampling reduces the stochastic contribution at rate \(b^{-1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_{\mathrm{crit}}(T)=C^2T/A^2\), with sampling-limited behavior below this boundary and deterministic-error-limited behavior above it.
